traditionalUse: Cooling agent for sunburn, heat rash, superficial burns and inflamed acne in Ayurvedic and household Kerala practice.
preparation: Slice a mature leaf, drain the yellow latex for 10 minutes, then scoop the clear inner gel and blend briefly.
application: Apply a thin layer to clean skin, leave 15-20 minutes, rinse with cool water. Use up to once daily.
safety: Discard the yellow latex — it is a skin irritant and laxative. Avoid on open or weeping wounds.
patchTest: Apply gel to the inner forearm and wait 24 hours before facial use.
references: Surjushe A. et al., Aloe vera: a short review, Indian J Dermatol, 2008
WHO Monographs on Selected Medicinal Plants, Vol. 1

traditionalUse: Anti-inflammatory and antimicrobial paste used before weddings and for blemishes across South India.
preparation: Mix 1/4 teaspoon Kasturi turmeric with 1 tablespoon yoghurt or raw honey into a smooth paste.
application: Apply to affected areas for 10 minutes, twice weekly, then rinse thoroughly.
safety: Culinary turmeric stains skin and fabric; Kasturi (wild) turmeric is preferred cosmetically. Not for broken skin.
patchTest: Test on the jawline for 24 hours — staining and contact dermatitis are both possible.
references: Vaughn AR. et al., Effects of turmeric on skin health, Phytother Res, 2016
Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India, Part I

traditionalUse: Traditional antibacterial and antifungal support for acne, folliculitis and itchy scalp conditions.
preparation: Boil a handful of fresh leaves in 500 ml water for 10 minutes, cool and strain to make a rinse; or grind leaves into a paste.
application: Use the cooled decoction as a final rinse, or apply the paste for 10 minutes twice weekly.
safety: Never ingest neem oil. Avoid during pregnancy. Can be drying with frequent use.
patchTest: 24-hour forearm test; neem is a common contact sensitiser.
references: Alzohairy MA., Therapeutic role of Azadirachta indica, Evid Based Complement Alternat Med, 2016

traditionalUse: Classic Kerala cooling paste for heat rash, prickly heat, redness and post-acne marks.
preparation: Grind a sandalwood stick on a wet stone, or mix 1 teaspoon pure powder with rose water.
application: Apply a thin layer, let it dry for 15 minutes, rinse with cool water. Two to three times weekly.
safety: Use genuine Santalum album powder; adulterated powders often contain dyes. Not for very dry skin.
references: Moy RL, Levenson C., Sandalwood album oil as a botanical therapeutic, J Clin Aesthet Dermatol, 2017

traditionalUse: Used as an antibacterial wash for breakouts and minor skin infections in household Ayurveda.
preparation: Steep 10-12 fresh leaves in hot water for 15 minutes; cool completely before use.
application: Use as a toner on cotton once daily, or add the paste to a clay mask weekly.
safety: Generally well tolerated. Avoid the concentrated essential oil undiluted.
references: Cohen MM., Tulsi - Ocimum sanctum: A herb for all reasons, J Ayurveda Integr Med, 2014

traditionalUse: Everyday Kerala emollient for dry skin, infant skin care and eczema-prone body skin.
preparation: Use cold-pressed virgin coconut oil, warmed slightly between the palms.
application: Apply to damp body skin after bathing. Avoid the face if you are acne-prone.
safety: Comedogenic on facial skin for many people. Excellent for the body, risky for the T-zone.
patchTest: 48-hour test on the jawline if you plan facial use.
references: Evangelista MTP. et al., The effect of topical virgin coconut oil on atopic dermatitis, Int J Dermatol, 2014

traditionalUse: Wound healing and scar softening herb; the source of modern 'cica' skincare.
preparation: Grind fresh leaves into a paste, or use a standardised centella extract serum.
application: Apply to healing marks once daily for 10-15 minutes, or use the extract morning and night.
safety: Avoid on active infected lesions. Discontinue if itching develops.
references: Bylka W. et al., Centella asiatica in dermatology, Phytother Res, 2014

traditionalUse: Gentle hydrating and calming toner used across Indian skincare traditions.
preparation: Steam-distilled rose water only; avoid fragrance-added rose 'water'.
application: Mist or pat onto clean skin morning and night before moisturiser.
safety: Check labels for added alcohol or synthetic fragrance which can irritate.
references: Mahboubi M., Rosa damascena as holy ancient herb with novel applications, J Tradit Complement Med, 2016
